From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Aurelia security discovery — post-call recap & next steps

Jack / Ivy — thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single action list to track: 

1) Current compliance posture (what you told us)
   - SOC 2: Type 2 in progress; SOC 2 readiness assessment completed Nov 2026; expected audit window Q4 2027.
   - HIPAA: PHI scope limited to a sub-account; BAAs in place with platform vendors; internal policies undergoing update.
   - GDPR: Data processing addendum drafted; DSR flows in design for product team.

2) Immediate asks from Aurelia (from call)
   - Fill our vendor security questionnaire (we attached the Redwood SVQ template) — target: 1 week.
   - Provide a high-level prod network diagram and data flow for EU/US boundaries.
   - Clarify encryption key ownership model and KMS options for private deployments.

3) Redwood commitments / deliverables
   - Share a short deck summarizing deployment modes, KMS options, and SOC 2 evidence types we can provide (attached).
   - Provide a private-deployment brief describing VPC/KMS/HSM options and audit log exports.
   - Gap map: we will map Aurelia’s current SOC controls to Redwood evidence artifacts and flag any additional compensating controls.

4) Proposed timeline / next touchpoints
   - Jack: complete the attached SVQ and prod network diagram by Wed 3/29.
   - Redwood (Rishi + Lauren): deliver the KMS/Private deployment brief and gap-map by Mon 4/4.
   - Joint follow-up: 30-minute call week of 4/5 to review the gap map and discuss potential scope for SOC expansion.

Attachments: redwood-aurelia-discovery-slide-deck.pdf, vendor-security-questionnaire.xlsx 

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite for the week-of-4/5 follow-up and Rishi will start drafting the technical brief.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124

We’ll target Wed 3/29 to return the completed questionnaire and any additional diagrams. Adding our security lead (security@aureliahealth.com) to keep the thread visible.

Subject: RE: Aurelia security discovery — post-call recap & next steps

Jack — appreciate the diagram, that’s helpful. Short technical clarifications and how Redwood can meet your KMS/HSM requirements: 

- Customer-managed keys: supported in Redwood Private via integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and customer HSMs for on-prem. You retain key ownership; we store only wrapped keys when applicable.
- Hosted API: default is Redwood-managed KMS; we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for Dedicated/Private tiers with additional compliance controls.
- Audit logs: we can export token-level and request-level audit logs to your S3/GCS bucket or push to a SIEM via secure forwarder.
- Data in transit / at rest: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 or equivalent at rest depending on deployment and quantization artifacts.

I’ve attached a short brief that outlines the private deployment model and KMS integration patterns (redwood-private-deployment-brief.pdf). If you want, we can propose two concrete options in the gap-map: (A) Redwood-managed KMS + strict access controls (faster), (B) Customer KMS/HSM + dedicated private tenancy (greater control).

Next steps for Rishi / Redwood: I’ll put together the option comparison and a short list of evidence artifacts we can provide for SOC review. Expect a draft by Mon 4/4.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-private-deployment-brief.pdf
